A lot of our client calls are timing out (30s) and our retry logic is amplifying the problem.

I've attached a short sample of logs and a snippet from our metrics. This is impacting active patient triage flows; we need an ETA and mitigation now. Are you able to route us onto an alternate model or fall back to the hosted smaller model?

I appreciate the quick help—this is high priority.

Subject: Re: sudden latencies and 5xx/429 spikes - quick triage notes

Thanks Monica — initial findings below. Copying Rajesh for transparency.

What we see (first-pass):
- Root cause signal: dedicated GPU pool "us-west-2-dedicated-a" hit sustained GPU memory pressure and epoch-driven eviction around 08:40–09:05 PDT. Evictions correlated with long-sequence inference jobs (avg seq len + kv-cache churn).
- Autoscaler lag: the horizontal autoscaler did trigger but backfill/boot time plus model warmup introduced a 90–120s window where requests queued -> 429s + 5xx due to OOMs in worker processes.
- Retry amplification: client-side retries (default retry policy) retried quickly, overwhelming backfill capacity and creating a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigations enacted (09:36–09:42 PDT):
1) Enabled temporary routing to dedicated-fallback model (smaller quantized variant) for 25% of traffic for Healthline via policy-based routing.
2) Increased pool target by adding 2 ephemeral GPUs from burst pool to the dedicated group (reduces queueing).
3) Adjusted autoscaler warmup threshold to prefer earlier scale (short term config tweak).
4) Set 429 circuit-breaker at the frontend ingress for the Healthline route to 10% to slow retries server-side.

Preliminary outcome: 5xx rate dropped from peak 18% to 3.6% within ~8 minutes after routing change; 429s dropped to ~7% then stabilized. We'll watch for the next 30 minutes for regression. Attached: svc-metrics-20280918-09-00.png (before/after).

Follow-ups (action items):
- Marcus: prepare compact postmortem with timeline & recommendation for persistent fix (pool sizing / pre-warm/kv-cache optimizations).
- Monica / Laura: coordinate customer comms and propose an interim credit for downtime window (we need to define impact window once Marcus timestamps logs).

I'll update when we have the postmortem skeleton.

- Aditya

Summary (for Execs):
- Incident: 5xx and 429 spike affecting Healthline AI in us-west-2 dedicated pool. Start: ~2028-09-18T08:45 PDT; mitigations applied by 09:42 PDT.
- Impact: short window of elevated errors affecting patient triage; estimated ~12 minutes of highest impact (08:45–08:57 PDT) and an extended degradation window until mitigations completed. Customer reports some timed-out flows.
- Root cause: GPU memory pressure + autoscaler warmup lag + retry amplification.
- Mitigation: temporary traffic routing to smaller quantized model (25% shift), added 2 burst GPUs, adjusted autoscaler warmup, enabled ingress-level 429 circuit breaker. Immediate metrics show error rate reduced to baseline within ~8 minutes of actions.

Actions requested from Execs:
1) Approve the proposed 10% service credit for September for Healthline (pending final impact window from Marcus).
2) Prioritize the "pre-warm + burst reservation" quick project with infra (estimated 2 sprints) to prevent warmup-driven backpressure on dedicated pools.
